To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synaptic activation of neurons in the brain- stem auditory nucleus nucleus magnocellulars (NM) results in an increase in the rate of protein synthesis by NM neurons.
synaptic activation of auditory nerve afferents is required for the transneuronal enhancement of protein synthesis in second-order auditory neurons.
synaptic transmission between the auditory nerve and nucleus magnocellular is required for the activity-dependent regulation of protein synthesis by NM neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the brain-stem nucleus, nucleus magnicellularis, responds to afferent activity.
the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in the auditory system.
the cellular mechanisms by which auditory nerve afferents influence the second-order neurons, the magnocellular neurons (NM) of the chick brainstem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
synaptic activation of NM neurons is necessary to increase protein synthesis in these neurons.
synaptic activation of auditory afferents in NM is required for enhanced protein synthesis in NM neurons.
the transneuronal effects of the auditory nerve on the protein synthesis of NM neurons are mediated by synaptic activity and that the trophic factor is released by the nerve terminals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

activity-dependent release of some “neurotrophin” from the auditory nerve, which is necessary for transneuronal protein synthesis in the chick brain-stem auditory nucleus, NM, does not depend on afferent activity per se, but rather on some other aspect of synaptic transmission.
synaptic activation is required for the enhancement of protein synthesis in auditory neurons of NM.
the auditory nerve is required for the regulation of protein synthesis by the second-order nucleus in the brain-stems auditory system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synaptic activation is required for transneuronal protein synthesis in the auditory brainstem of the chick.
the brainstem auditory system is a great model to study how the brain is wired and how it is maintained.
synaptic activity is required for the transneuronal induction of protein synthesis, and that this induction is mediated by a diffusible substance released from the auditory nerve.
